If that is not what you meant, clarify the prompt.`;\n}\n\nfunction wikipediaClarificationMessage(summary, language) {\n  const title = summary && summary.title ? summary.title : \"the top result\";\n  if (language === \"ru\") {\n    return `Похоже, вы имели в виду «${title}». Уточните, отвечать по этой статье Wikipedia?`;\n  }\n  if (language === \"zh\") {\n    return `你是指“${title}”吗？请确认后我再根据这篇 Wikipedia 文章回答。`;\n  }\n  if (language === \"hi\") {\n    return `क्या आपका मतलब \"${title}\" था? Please clarify before I answer from that Wikipedia article.`;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Wikidata-backed fact reasoning pipeline (issue #127).\n//\n// Rather than matching against hardcoded summaries in `data/seed/facts.lino`,\n// fact questions (\"what is the capital of X?\", \"столица X\", \"X की राजधानी\",\n// \"X的首都\") are parsed into a structured query\n// `{ relation, subjectTerm, language, forceFresh }`. The query is then\n// resolved against:\n//\n//   1. An in-memory cache (1-week TTL) keyed by `relation:subject:language`.\n//      The cache is pre-warmed from the seed `FACTS` entries so the test\n//      matrix stays deterministic offline.\n//   2. Wikidata `wbgetentities` to fetch the property claim (P36 = capital,\n//      P1082 = population, P38 = currency, P37 = official language, P30 =\n//      continent, P2046 = area, P35 = head of state, P6 = head of government).\n//   4. Detected in all\n// four supported languages plus a couple of common English phrasings.\nconst FORCE_FRESH_MARKERS = [\n  \"fresh\",\n  \"no cache\",\n  \"no-cache\",\n  \"without cache\",\n  \"skip cache\",\n  \"ignore cache\",\n  \"refresh\",\n  \"не из кэша\",\n  \"не из кеша\",\n  \"без кэша\",\n  \"без кеша\",\n  \"обнови\",\n  \"свежий ответ\",\n  \"свежие данные\",\n  \"ताज़ा\",\n  \"ताज़े\",\n  \"बिना कैश\",\n  \"नया जवाब\",\n  \"刷新\",\n  \"新鲜\",\n  \"不要缓存\",\n  \"不用缓存\",\n];\n\nfunction shouldForceFresh(normalized, prompt) {\n  const lowerPrompt = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  return FORCE_FRESH_MARKERS.some(\n    (marker) => normalized.includes(marker) || lowerPrompt.includes(marker),\n  );\n}\n\n// Multilingual relation patterns. Order matters: longer prefixes first.\nconst SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES = [\n  \"the country called \",\n  \"the country \",\n  \"country \",\n  \"the city of \",\n  \"the city \",\n  \"city of \",\n  \"country called \",\n  \"republic of \",\n  \"kingdom of \",\n  \"is \",\n  \"in \",\n  \"of the \",\n  \"of \",\n  \"страна \",\n  \"страны \",\n  \"стране \",\n  \"страну \",\n];\n\nfunction trimSubjectTerm(raw) {\n  let value = String(raw || \"\")\n    .replace(/[«»\"'`“”„‟‹›]+/g, \"\")\n    .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n    .trim();\n  let changed = true;\n  while (changed) {\n    changed = false;\n    const lower = value.toLowerCase();\n    for (const prefix of SUBJECT_TRIM_PREFIXES) {\n      if (lower.startsWith(prefix)) {\n        value = value.slice(prefix.length).trim();\n        changed = true;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\nfunction parseFactQuestion(prompt, normalized) {\n  const text = String(prompt || \"\");\n  if (!text.trim()) return null;\n  for (const pattern of FACT_QUESTION_PATTERNS) {\n    for (const regex of pattern.extract) {\n      const match = regex.exec(text);\n      if (!match) continue;\n      const subjectTerm = trimSubjectTerm(match[1]);\n      if (!subjectTerm) continue;\n      // Reject single-letter or pure-punctuation captures so we don't fire\n      // on noise like \"x.\" or \"?\".\n      if (subjectTerm.length < 2 && !/[Ѐ-鿿]/.test(subjectTerm)) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      return {\n        relation: pattern.relation,\n        subjectTerm,\n        language: detectLanguage(prompt),\n        forceFresh: shouldForceFresh(normalized, prompt),\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n// In-memory cache. Keyed by `relation:subject_normalized:language`. The TTL\n// matches the user-requested 1 week. Pre-warmed from FACTS at init() so the\n// offline test matrix sees the same starting cache the Rust solver does.\nconst FACT_QUERY_CACHE = new Map();\nconst FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n\nfunction factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  return [\n    String(relation || \"\").toLowerCase(),\n    String(subjectTerm || \"\")\n      .toLowerCase()\n      .replace(/\\s+/g, \" \")\n      .trim(),\n    String(language || \"en\").toLowerCase(),\n  ].join(\":\");\n}\n\nfunction factCacheGet(relation, subjectTerm, language) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const entry = FACT_QUERY_CACHE.get(key);\n  if (!entry) return null;\n  if (\n    entry.expiresAt &&\n    typeof entry.expiresAt === \"number\" &&\n    entry.expiresAt < Date.now()\n  ) {\n    FACT_QUERY_CACHE.delete(key);\n    return null;\n  }\n  return entry;\n}\n\nfunction factCachePut(relation, subjectTerm, language, value) {\n  const key = factCacheKey(relation, subjectTerm, language);\n  const ttl = typeof value.ttlMs === \"number\" ? value.ttlMs : FACT_QUERY_TTL_MS;\n  const entry = Object.assign({}, value, {\n    expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl,\n  });\n  FACT_QUERY_CACHE.set(key, entry);\n  return entry;\n}\n\n// Pre-warm the runtime cache from the seed `facts.lino`. We try WASM first and only\n  // fall back to the JS implementation when the worker booted in\n  // `js fallback` mode (e.g. WASM disabled in the browser).\n  const wasmFused = wasmReciprocalRankFusion(perProviderResults);\n  if (wasmFused !== null) {\n    return wasmFused;\n  }\n  // Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher 2009: score(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d)).\n  const fused = new Map();\n  for (const provider of perProviderResults) {\n    const list = Array.isArray(provider.results) ? provider.results : [];\n    list.forEach((item, index) => {\n      if (!item || !item.url) return;\n      const rank = index + 1;\n      const score = 1 / (k + rank);\n      const existing = fused.get(item.url);\n      if (existing) {\n        existing.score += score;\n        existing.providers.push({ id: provider.id, rank });\n        if (!existing.title && item.title) existing.title = item.title;\n        if (!existing.excerpt && item.excerpt) existing.excerpt = item.excerpt;\n      } else {\n        fused.set(item.url, {\n          url: item.url,\n          title: item.title || item.url,\n          excerpt: item.excerpt || \"\",\n          score,\n          providers: [{ id: provider.id, rank }],\n        });\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  return Array.from(fused.values()).sort((a, b) => {\n    if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;\n    return b.providers.length - a.providers.length;\n  });\n}\n\n// Issue #153/#180: identify \"the same entity\" returned by different providers\n// so the fused list shows one bullet with the other URLs collapsed under\n// \"Other sources:\". byUrl.get(url);\n    if (!existing || rank(item) > rank(existing)) {\n      byUrl.set(url, item);\n    }\n  }\n  for (const provider of perProvider) {\n    if (!provider || !Array.isArray(provider.results)) continue;\n    for (const item of provider.results) {\n      if (!item || !item.url) continue;\n      record(item.url, item);\n      // Wikidata results carry the \").trim();\n}\n\nfunction evidenceFromUserContext(userContext) {\n  if (!userContext || typeof userContext !== \"object\") return [];\n  const evidence = [];\n  const fields = [\n    [\"uiLanguage\", We emit a deterministic, offline formalization\n// here (so the trace is stable even when no APIs are reachable) and, when a\n// downstream handler resolves the object to a Wikidata/Wikipedia/Wiktionary\n// item, we emit a second `formalize_resolved` step with the real ids. {\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  const raw = String(prompt || \"\");\n  const rawLower = String(prompt || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb, op } of FORMALIZATION_VERBS) {\n    if (haystack.startsWith(verb + \" \") || haystack === verb) {\n      return {\n        op,\n        verb,\n        objectText: haystack === verb ? \"\" : normalized.slice(verb.length),\n        interpretations: [],\n      };\n    }\n    if (rawLower.startsWith(verb + \" \") || rawLower === verb) {\n      return {\n        op,\n        verb,\n        objectText: rawLower === verb ? \"\" : raw.slice(verb.length),\n        interpretations: [],\n      };\n    }\n    if (haystack.includes(\" \" + verb + \" \")) {\n      return { op, verb, objectText: null, interpretations: [] };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt) {\n  const matches = FORMALIZATION_VERBS\n    .map((entry) => {\n      const match = fuzzyPrefixMatch(prompt, entry.verb);\n      return match ? Object.assign({ entry }, match) : null;\n    })\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .sort((left, right) =>\n      left.typoCount - right.typoCount || right.end - left.end,\n    );\n  const best = matches[0];\n  if (!best) return null;\n  const peers = matches.filter(\n    (match) => match.typoCount === best.typoCount && match.end === best.end,\n  );\n  if (peers.length > 1) {\n    return {\n      ambiguous: true,\n      suggestions: peers.map((match) => match.entry.verb),\n      interpretations: [],\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    op: best.entry.op,\n    verb: best.entry.verb,\n    objectText: String(prompt || \"\").slice(best.end),\n    interpretations: [best.interpretation],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) {\n  return exactFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized) || fuzzyFormalizationMatch(prompt);\n}\n\nfunction objectForFormalization(prompt, normalized, match) {\n  // For search-style ops we extract the explicit query the same way the web\n  // search handler does. For other ops we keep the prompt body that follows\n  // the detected verb so the tuple shows what the user is asking about.\n  const op = match && match.op;\n  if (op === \"OP:search\" || op === \"OP:lookup\") {\n    const query = extractWebSearchQuery(prompt, normalized);\n    if (query) return query;\n  }\n  if (op === \"OP:procedure\") {\n    const task = extractProceduralHowToTask(normalized);\n    if (task) return task.task;\n  }\n  const haystack = String(normalized || \"\").toLowerCase();\n  for (const { verb } of FORMALIZATION_VERBS) {\n    if (haystack.startsWith(verb + \" \")) {\n      return cleanSearchQuery(normalized.slice(verb.length));\n    }\n  }\n  if (match && typeof match.objectText === \"string\") {\n    return cleanSearchQuery(match.objectText);\n  }\n  return cleanSearchQuery(normalized || \"\");\n}\n\nfunction virtualObjectId(term) {\n  const trimmed = String(term || \"\").trim();\n  if (!trimmed) return \"?\";\n  return `?${trimmed}`;\n}\n\nfunction formatFormalizationTuple(parts) {\n  return `(${parts.filter(Boolean).join(\" \")})`;\n}\n\nfunction buildFormalization(prompt, normalized) {\n  const match = detectFormalizationMatch(prompt, normalized);\n  if (!match || match.ambiguous) {\n    const fallback = normalized || \"(empty)\";\n    return {\n      raw: String(prompt || \"\"),\n      subject: \"@USER\",\n      verb: \"OP:express\",\n      object: virtualObjectId(fallback),\n      tuple: formatFormalizationTuple([\"@USER\", \"OP:express\", virtualObjectId(fallback)]),\n      needsClarification: Boolean(match && match.ambiguous),\n      suggestions: match && match.suggestions ? #221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Pre-compiled offline dictionary\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (new): runs the cached\n  pipeline against the full seed list and emits\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json`. Schema:\n\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"version\": 1,\n    \"entries\": …,\n    \"alias_count\": …,\n    \"by_lemma\": {\n      \"en\": { \"tomato\": { \"ru\": \"помидор\", \"hi\": \"टमाटर\", \"zh\": \"番茄\" } },\n      \"ru\": { \"помидор\": { \"en\": \"tomato\" } }\n    },\n    \"aliases\": {\n      \"ru\": { \"помидора\": \"помидор\", \"помидору\": \"помидор\", … },\n      \"en\": { \"tomatoes\": \"tomato\", … }\n    }\n  }\n  ```\n\n  Inflection forms are generated deterministically — Russian\n  declension suffixes by ending class and English plural rules — so\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` resolves to `tomato` without\n  another network call.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `loadTranslationDictionary()` fetches\n  the JSON above during `init()` (alongside the existing seed loader),\n  and `translateSurface` consults `lookupDictionary(...)` before\n  falling back to the hand-curated registry / placeholder. The fetch\n  is same-origin (no CORS), and the JSON ships as a static asset.\n- The browser worker can therefore resolve every common noun in the\n  seed list **without** crossing the network, while keeping the\n  existing registry as a back-up for greeting phrases.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; [2026-05-22T00:50:03.387Z] [INFO]     "newString": "### Single-file offline dictionary (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `data/seed/translations.lino` (new): the canonical 128-entry\n  common-noun dictionary, indented Links Notation, ~1,300 lines.\n  Embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the\n  browser worker through the existing seed loader. One file → one\n  source of truth across Rust, CLI, browser, and tests.\n  Schema (one record per lemma):\n\n  ```text\n  translation_en_tomato\n    language \"en\"\n    lemma \"tomato\"\n    aliases \"tomato|tomatoes\"\n    target \"ru\"\n      surface \"помидор\"\n    target \"hi\"\n      surface \"टमाटर\"\n    target \"zh\"\n      surface \"番茄\"\n  ```\n\n  `src/translation/dictionary.rs` parses the file once at startup\n  (`OnceLock`) into a bidirectional `(language, surface_lower) →\n  entry` map plus a reverse `(target_lang, target_surface_lower) →\n  entry` map. The reverse map lets a single en→ru entry cover both\n  directions, keeping the 128-entry cap meaningful.\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (revised): runs the\n  cached pipeline against the seed list and writes\n  `data/seed/translations.lino` instead of a JSON file. Inflection\n  forms are generated deterministically — Russian declension suffixes\n  by ending class and English plural rules — so `Переведи \"помидоры\"\n  на английский.` still resolves to `tomato` via the alias index.\n\n### Generic semantic-key cache (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` now routes URLs to per-source folders by\n  the **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the cache\n  is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows\n  beyond translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the\n  same buckets so we never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n### Browser worker (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: a new `extractTranslations` parser mirrors\n  the Rust `Dictionary::parse` (same bidirectional index, same alias\n  handling). It runs as part of the standard `buildSeed` step so the\n  worker hydrates the dictionary alongside facts, projects, concepts,\n  and intent routing — no separate fetch, no JSON glue.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` is now\n  populated directly from `seed.translations`; `lookupDictionary`\n  consults the forward map first and falls back to the reverse map\n  for the opposite direction. The previous JSON loader and\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` were deleted.\n- Because the dictionary is capped at 128 entries (R221.cap) and most\n  prompts will never hit it, the architecture stays mobile-friendly:\n  uncached lookups fall through to the live Wiktionary / Wikidata\n  APIs over `fetch()` instead of shipping a precomputed corpus.",
[2026-05-22T00:50:03.387Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# Issue 221 Case Study\n\n## Scope\n\nUmbrella issue: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/221>\n\nBranch: `issue-221-77aad836fb28`\nPull request: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/222>\n\nIssue #221 reports that the browser demo still produces fake\nplaceholders for common nouns the predecessor case study #218 did not\ncover:\n\n```\nU: Переведи \"яблоко\" на английский.\nA: \"apple\"\nU: Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] огурец\"\nU: Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.\nA: \"[en] помидор\"\n```\n\nThe umbrella requirement (verbatim, from the issue): *\"We must stop\nfaking translation, and actually implement it for all possible words we\ncan find in wikipedia, wikidata, wiktionary, and actually use APIs.\"*\n\nIn other words, #218 fixed the **single-noun apple** case; #221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Cache seed list expanded from 1 noun to 71×4 + 71 pairs; `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` ships the result as `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` so the browser worker can resolve common nouns without CORS-blocked API calls. |\n| 2026-05-21 | `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` verbose tracing added to the Rust pipeline (issue #218 \"Future work\" item). |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) flags 3,000+ files in the diff and asks for a lightweight architecture. Cache is reorganised by **semantic data type** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`) and gitignored; the JSON dictionary is replaced by a single 128-entry **`data/seed/translations.lino`** file embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the browser worker through the standard seed loader. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n6. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n   pinned down.\n7. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Pre-compiled offline dictionary\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (new): runs the cached\n  pipeline against the full seed list and emits\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json`. Schema:\n\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"version\": 1,\n    \"entries\": …,\n    \"alias_count\": …,\n    \"by_lemma\": {\n      \"en\": { \"tomato\": { \"ru\": \"помидор\", \"hi\": \"टमाटर\", \"zh\": \"番茄\" } },\n      \"ru\": { \"помидор\": { \"en\": \"tomato\" } }\n    },\n    \"aliases\": {\n      \"ru\": { \"помидора\": \"помидор\", \"помидору\": \"помидор\", … },\n      \"en\": { \"tomatoes\": \"tomato\", … }\n    }\n  }\n  ```\n\n  Inflection forms are generated deterministically — Russian\n  declension suffixes by ending class and English plural rules — so\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` resolves to `tomato` without\n  another network call.\n\n### Browser worker\n\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `loadTranslationDictionary()` fetches\n  the JSON above during `init()` (alongside the existing seed loader),\n  and `translateSurface` consults `lookupDictionary(...)` before\n  falling back to the hand-curated registry / placeholder. The fetch\n  is same-origin (no CORS), and the JSON ships as a static asset.\n- The browser worker can therefore resolve every common noun in the\n  seed list **without** crossing the network, while keeping the\n  existing registry as a back-up for greeting phrases.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; three new `issue_221_*` tests pass.\n- `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1 cargo run --release --example refresh_translation_cache`\n  — no gaps in the new seed list (rerun once a quarter to refresh).\n- `cargo run --release --example build_translation_dictionary` —\n  rebuilds `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` from the cache.\n- `npm --prefix tests/e2e run test:local -- tests/issue-221.spec.js` —\n  browser worker regressions pass.\n\n## Upstream-issue reports\n\nNone filed. Same diagnosis as #218 applies: Wiktionary serves correct\ndata, Wikidata serves correct lexemes, the gaps were entirely in our\nseeding pipeline. The polysemy edge cases that surfaced during seeding\n(e.g. `milk` → `доить` because the Wikidata lexeme query returned the\nverb first) are catalogued in `online-research.md` and tracked in the\n\"Future work\" section below — the dictionary captures the right\nsurface for nouns explicitly, side-stepping the issue for the demo.\n\n## Future work\n\n- **Lexeme disambiguation** — the SPARQL query in\n  `src/translation/wikidata.rs` should restrict P5137 joins by\n  lexical category (noun ↔ noun) so `milk` resolves to `молоко`\n  instead of `доить`. Tracked under the polysemy follow-up.\n- **Live Wiktionary fetch in the browser** — the worker can still\n  reach `*.wiktionary.org/w/api.php?...&origin=*` for words not in\n  the dictionary. Now that the dictionary infrastructure exists we\n  can layer a tiny CORS-aware wikitext parser on top.\n- **Sentence-level translation** — the issue asks for \"text of any\n  size\". The current pipeline plus dictionary covers single words and\n  short greetings. A proper sentence pipeline (tokenize → translate\n  per-token → re-inflect via Wiktionary grammar tables) is the\n  long-form follow-up. Tracked in the \"согласованность\" comment in\n  issue #221.\n",

#221 demands\nthat the **same machinery works for any common noun**, in any direction\nbetween the supported languages, in **both** the Rust CLI and the\nbrowser demo, *without LLMs*.\n\n## Timeline\n\n| Date (UTC) | Event |\n| --- | --- |\n| 2026-05-19 | PR #208 lands the Wiktionary + Wikidata translation pipeline. |\n| 2026-05-21 | PR #211 fixes translation handler precedence and adds the compositional ru→en fallback. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #216 — `translate apple to russian` returns `[ru]`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #217 — `переведи «яблоко» на английский` returns `\"[en] яблоко\"`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Umbrella issue #218 opened; PR #219 fixes the apple noun for all four supported languages and lands a multilingual coverage CI guard. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Demo report #221 — the same fix does not cover `помидор` / `огурец` and the request escalates to **all** common nouns plus *texts of any size*. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Branch `issue-221-77aad836fb28` cut; PR #222 prepared. |\n| 2026-05-21 | CLI reproduction confirms the placeholder lives in two places: the offline cache only has `яблоко`, and the browser registry only has `apple`. |\n| 2026-05-21 | Cache seed list expanded from 1 noun to 71×4 + 71 pairs; `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` ships the result as `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` so the browser worker can resolve common nouns without CORS-blocked API calls. |\n| 2026-05-21 | `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` verbose tracing added to the Rust pipeline (issue #218 \"Future work\" item). |\n| 2026-05-22 | PR #222 review (konard) flags 3,000+ files in the diff and asks for a lightweight architecture. Cache is reorganised by **semantic data type** (`wikidata-cache/{search,entities,query,sparql}/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, `http-cache/misc/`) and gitignored; the JSON dictionary is replaced by a single 128-entry **`data/seed/translations.lino`** file embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the browser worker through the standard seed loader. |\n\n## Requirements (from issue #221)\n\n1. Stop faking translation — no `[en] X` / `[ru] X` placeholders for\n   any common noun in any supported direction.\n2. Use Wikipedia, Wikidata, and Wiktionary as the only sources of\n   meaning — the symbolic AI pipeline must remain LLM-free.\n3. Follow the *source → meta → target* flow already proven in #218:\n   `formalize(source) → meaning_id (Q/L/sense) → deformalize(target)`.\n4. Solve everything in a single pull request that **actually works**,\n   not just for one phrase but for arbitrary text size.\n5. Compile all logs and data into `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/`,\n   reconstruct the timeline, list every requirement, find every root\n   cause, and propose solutions. Search externally for additional data.\n6. Add debug output and a verbose mode if a root cause cannot yet be\n   pinned down.\n7. Report upstream defects against any external repo (Wiktionary,\n   Wikidata, etc.) that surface during investigation.\n\n## Artifacts\n\nLocal artifacts captured during investigation live under `raw-data/`:\n\n- `repro-pomidor-before-fix.txt`, `repro-ogurec-before-fix.txt` — CLI\n  reproductions before any change. Offline cache miss → `[en] помидор`.\n- `repro-pomidor-live-api.txt`, `repro-ogurec-live-api.txt` — same\n  prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`. Pipeline resolves\n  помидор→tomato and огурец→cucumber correctly, proving the algorithm\n  works and the gap is data-seeding-only.\n- `test-before-fix.txt` — output of the new `issue_221_*` tests before\n  any seeding change, showing two failures (картофель/potato) and one\n  pass (помидор/огурец, because earlier live-API runs had already\n  warmed those entries).\n\n`online-research.md` collects the external references used while\ndiagnosing the bug (Wiktionary CORS policy, MediaWiki `origin=*`\nconvention, Wikidata SPARQL endpoint behaviour for polysemous lexemes).\n\n## Root Causes\n\n1. **Offline cache only contained one noun (`яблоко` / `apple`).**\n   `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` was the single source of\n   ground-truth data fed to the offline pipeline, and PR #219 added\n   only the apple pair. Every other common noun returned an `HttpError::\n   Transport(... cache miss for {url} and offline mode is active)`,\n   which the handler renders as `[en] помидор`. Verified by re-running\n   the same prompt with `FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1` — the pipeline succeeds\n   immediately (logs in `raw-data/repro-*-live-api.log`).\n2. **Browser worker only consulted a hand-curated registry.**\n   `TRANSLATION_MEANING_REGISTRY` in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` was\n   built up phrase-by-phrase. Words missing from the registry fell\n   through to `[${target}] ${surface}` (line 3905 pre-fix). The Rust\n   pipeline never runs in the browser — the worker is the only code\n   that handles in-browser translation, and the existing infrastructure\n   for live Wiktionary calls (e.g. `fetchWiktionaryEntry`) is only used\n   for the *external lookup* fallback, not for translation.\n3. **No automated bridge between the Rust ground truth and the JS\n   worker.** Even when PR #219 added the apple noun in both places, the\n   data lived in two unrelated source files; nothing kept them in sync.\n4. **No verbose mode in the pipeline.** When tests failed, the only\n   signal was a single line of output. Issue #218 explicitly listed\n   `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1` as future work.\n\n## Fixes\n\n### Rust core\n\n- `src/translation/pipeline.rs`: add `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`\n  verbose tracing through every stage (`stage1` source-edition,\n  reverse, variants, Wikidata upgrade, compositional fallback). When\n  enabled, every translation prints stage-by-stage to stderr so\n  cache-miss vs sparse-Wiktionary-table vs polysemy can be\n  distinguished in a single run.\n- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs`: grow the seed list from one\n  noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 targets and 71 Russian\n  nouns × 1 target** — every word listed in the demo / regression set\n  the issue exemplifies. `pairs` is now built procedurally so future\n  expansions stay readable.\n\n### Single-file offline dictionary (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `data/seed/translations.lino` (new): the canonical 128-entry\n  common-noun dictionary, indented Links Notation, ~1,300 lines.\n  Embedded into the Rust binary via `include_str!` and fetched by the\n  browser worker through the existing seed loader. One file → one\n  source of truth across Rust, CLI, browser, and tests.\n  Schema (one record per lemma):\n\n  ```text\n  translation_en_tomato\n    language \"en\"\n    lemma \"tomato\"\n    aliases \"tomato|tomatoes\"\n    target \"ru\"\n      surface \"помидор\"\n    target \"hi\"\n      surface \"टमाटर\"\n    target \"zh\"\n      surface \"番茄\"\n  ```\n\n  `src/translation/dictionary.rs` parses the file once at startup\n  (`OnceLock`) into a bidirectional `(language, surface_lower) →\n  entry` map plus a reverse `(target_lang, target_surface_lower) →\n  entry` map. The reverse map lets a single en→ru entry cover both\n  directions, keeping the 128-entry cap meaningful.\n\n- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (revised): runs the\n  cached pipeline against the seed list and writes\n  `data/seed/translations.lino` instead of a JSON file. Inflection\n  forms are generated deterministically — Russian declension suffixes\n  by ending class and English plural rules — so `Переведи \"помидоры\"\n  на английский.` still resolves to `tomato` via the alias index.\n\n### Generic semantic-key cache (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/translation/cache.rs` now routes URLs to per-source folders by\n  the **kind of data** they carry, not by URL hash:\n\n  | URL pattern | Cache folder |\n  | --- | --- |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/search/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbgetentities` | `data/wikidata-cache/entities/` |\n  | `wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=query` | `data/wikidata-cache/query/` |\n  | `query.wikidata.org/sparql` | `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` |\n  | `<lang>.wiktionary.org` | `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/` |\n  | anything else | `data/http-cache/misc/` |\n\n  Every folder under `data/` listed above is gitignored — the cache\n  is a local accelerator, not pre-seeded data. Formalisation flows\n  beyond translation (entity resolution, fact lookup, etc.) reuse the\n  same buckets so we never grow a per-feature cache silo again.\n\n### Browser worker (revised 2026-05-22)\n\n- `src/web/seed_loader.js`: a new `extractTranslations` parser mirrors\n  the Rust `Dictionary::parse` (same bidirectional index, same alias\n  handling). It runs as part of the standard `buildSeed` step so the\n  worker hydrates the dictionary alongside facts, projects, concepts,\n  and intent routing — no separate fetch, no JSON glue.\n- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`: `TRANSLATION_DICTIONARY` is now\n  populated directly from `seed.translations`; `lookupDictionary`\n  consults the forward map first and falls back to the reverse map\n  for the opposite direction. The previous JSON loader and\n  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json` were deleted.\n- Because the dictionary is capped at 128 entries (R221.cap) and most\n  prompts will never hit it, the architecture stays mobile-friendly:\n  uncached lookups fall through to the live Wiktionary / Wikidata\n  APIs over `fetch()` instead of shipping a precomputed corpus.\n\n### Tests\n\n- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs`: three new tests\n  — `issue_221_common_russian_nouns_translate_to_english`,\n  `issue_221_common_english_nouns_translate_to_russian`, and\n  `issue_221_unquoted_common_noun_works_in_all_languages` — fail\n  loudly when any of помидор/огурец/картофель/морковь/хлеб/вода or\n  their English counterparts return a placeholder.\n- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js`: Playwright coverage for the\n  browser worker — same prompts as the Rust tests, plus the round-trip\n  `ru→en→ru` to prove the dictionary keeps semantics symmetric.\n\n## Before / After\n\n| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `Переведи \"помидор\" на английский.` | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n| `Переведи \"огурец\" на английский.` | `\"[en] огурец\"` | `\"cucumber\"` |\n| `переведи \"картофель\" на английский` | `\"[en] картофель\"` | `\"potato\"` |\n| `translate \"tomato\" to russian` | `\"[ru] tomato\"` | `\"помидор\"` |\n| `translate \"carrot\" to russian` | `\"[ru] carrot\"` | `\"морковь\"` |\n| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `\"[en] помидор\"` | `\"tomato\"` |\n\nRaw CLI reproductions are in `raw-data/repro-*-before-fix.txt` and\n`raw-data/repro-*-live-api.txt`.\n\n## Verification\n\n- `cargo build --release` — clean.\n- `cargo test --release --test unit translation_via_links` — issue\n  #218 tests still pass; [2026-05-22T00:50:33.800Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "# Issue 221 — Online Research Notes\n\nExternal references collected while diagnosing the umbrella common-noun\ntranslation gap reported in issue #221. The order mirrors the\ninvestigation timeline; each reference was followed against live\nendpoints before any code change.\n\n## Wiktionary API\n\n- **`action=parse&prop=wikitext`** — the pipeline pulls raw wikitext\n  for every page rather than the rendered HTML. The wikitext is the\n  only place where the `{{trans-top}}` / `{{перев-блок}}` sense\n  blocks are stable, since rendered HTML strips template metadata.\n- **CORS** — MediaWiki accepts `&origin=*` for anonymous read-only\n  GETs across all `*.wiktionary.org` editions. This is what\n  `fetchWiktionaryEntry` already uses for the external lookup\n  fallback. We **could** add live translation fetch in the worker on\n  top of this, but the current pull request opts for a pre-compiled\n  dictionary because the demo must work without leaking the\n  user's browsing patterns to Wikimedia. See PR #222 discussion.\n- **Translation subpages** — high-traffic English entries (e.g.\n  `apple`, `book`, `milk`) keep translation tables on a `/translations`\n  subpage referenced by `{{see translation subpage|...}}`. The Rust\n  pipeline already tries this fallback (`pipeline.rs` stage 1a).\n\n## Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join\n\n- **P5137** (`item for this sense`) is the canonical link from a\n  Wiktionary sense to a language-neutral Q-item. Joining two\n  lexemes through P5137 gives us a deterministic\n  `meaning_id (Q…)` regardless of which side served the trigger.\n- **Polysemy gotcha** — when a single surface form has both noun and\n  verb lexemes (e.g. English `milk` → noun `L4514` and verb\n  `L4514-S1`), the SPARQL query returns whichever lexeme appears\n  first. The current code path picks `L4514` and follows its sole\n  P5137 sense to whatever Wikidata calls the canonical Russian form,\n  landing on `доить` (the verb \"to milk\") instead of `молоко`. This\n  is a **known limitation** flagged in the case-study future work;\n  the dictionary work-around captures `molokó` directly for the\n  demo.\n- **502 errors** — the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint occasionally returns\n  HTTP 502 under load. The pipeline records the error in the\n  provenance trace and falls back to the Wiktionary block-level\n  result instead of failing the whole translation.\n\n## Russian Wiktionary specifics\n\n- The `=== Перевод ===` section is the reverse-lookup anchor. The\n  Russian edition is the densest source of `ru → other` data because\n  English Wiktionary's `ru:` columns are often sparse for\n  intermediate-frequency nouns.\n- Inflection templates (`{{сущ-ru|...}}`) carry the full declension\n  paradigm in wikitext. We do **not** parse them in this PR — the\n  alias generator hard-codes the common suffix tables — but\n  parsing them is the right long-term answer for issues like\n  `Переведи \"помидоры\" на английский.` (plural form).\n\n## Browser CORS constraints\n\n- Web workers run in the same origin as the host page (GitHub\n  Pages: `link-assistant.github.io`). They can `fetch()` any\n  same-origin asset (the seed bundles, the WASM blob, and now\n  `translation-dictionary.json`).\n- Cross-origin fetches succeed only when the remote server emits\n  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Wiktionary's `api.php` does so\n  when you pass `&origin=*`. So a live fallback is technically\n  possible — see the \"Future work\" section in the README.\n\n## Related upstream issues\n\n- Wikimedia phabricator T241992 — long-standing request to include\n  P5137 senses in `wbsearchentities`. If it ever lands, our\n  formalize step can hit a single API and skip the Wiktionary\n  wikitext parse for many words.\n- Wiktionary T118720 — the inflection-template normalization\n  request that would make plural / case forms machine-extractable.\n  Tracking issue, not actionable from our side.\n",

Shared between the Rust pipeline\n/// and the browser worker (which fetches the same file at runtime).\npub const SOURCE_TEXT: &str = include_str!(\"../../data/seed/translations.lino\");\n\n/// One dictionary entry: a lemma in a source language with its\n/// translations into one or more target languages.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DictionaryEntry {\n    pub language: String,\n    pub lemma: String,\n    pub aliases: Vec<String>,\n    pub targets: HashMap<String, String>,\n}\n\n/// Parsed dictionary, indexed by `(language, surface_lower)` →\n/// canonical entry. The same entry is registered under the canonical\n/// lemma and every alias so callers can look up inflected forms\n/// directly.\n///\n/// `reverse` mirrors every `(target_lang, target_surface_lower)` back to\n/// the owning source entry so that, given an en→ru entry for\n/// `thank you → спасибо`, `lookup(\"спасибо\", \"ru\", \"en\")` succeeds\n/// without a second dictionary entry. parse(text: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut entries: HashMap<(String, String), DictionaryEntry> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut reverse: HashMap<(String, String), DictionaryEntry> = HashMap::new();\n        let mut current: Option<DictionaryEntry> = None;\n        let mut current_target: Option<String> = None;\n\n        for raw_line in text.lines() {\n            if raw_line.trim().is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let indent = raw_line.bytes().take_while(|b| *b == b' ').count();\n            let content = &raw_line[indent..];\n Earlier revisions of this module hashed the full URL and dumped 3 500+\n//! tiny `.body` / `.url` files into a single `data/translation-cache/`\n//! directory. That made the pull request unreviewable and locked the\n//! cache to one consumer (translation). Issue #221 reshaped the cache so\n//! that:\n//!\n//! - **Wikidata** responses land under `data/wikidata-cache/` keyed by\n//!   the Q-id or Lexeme-id mentioned in the URL.\n//! - **Wiktionary** wikitext lands under `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`\n//!   keyed by the page title.\n//! - **SPARQL** queries land under `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` keyed by\n//!   a short hash, because there is no natural semantic name for a SPARQL\n//!   string.\n//! - **Everything else** still uses a URL-hash filename, but in a\n//!   dedicated `data/http-cache/misc/` bucket. Unrecognised hosts should\n//!   be rare in practice — the cache is intentionally narrow.\n//!\n//! This layout lets other formalization paths reuse the same Wikidata or\n//! Wiktionary lookups without duplicating bytes. It also keeps each\n//! directory small and human-readable (`grep -R apple\n//! data/wiktionary-cache/` works).\n//!\n//! !url.contains(\"wikidata.org\") {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let query_start = url.find('?')?;\n    let query = &url[query_start + 1..];\n    let mut action: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut srsearch: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut ids: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut sparql: Option<String> = None;\n    let mut titles: Option<String> = None;\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n }\n}\n\nfn percent_decode(value: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = value.as_bytes();\n    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n [2026-05-22T00:59:25.142Z] [INFO]   ✅ Found pull request #222: "Generalize translation pipeline + dictionary for all common nouns (issue #221)"
[2026-05-22T00:59:25.502Z] [STDOUT] ## Summary

Fixes #221 — stops faking translation for common nouns by generalizing
the existing Wiktionary + Wikidata pipeline (proven on `apple` in PR #219)
to **every common noun** in the demo's seed set, in both the Rust CLI and
the browser worker, with no LLM in the loop.

The full investigation lives in `docs/case-studies/issue-221/` (timeline,
seven verbatim issue requirements, four root causes, fixes, before/after
table, verification commands, upstream defect notes, and online research
on Wiktionary CORS / Wikidata SPARQL polysemy).

## Changes

### Rust core
- `src/translation/pipeline.rs` — `FORMAL_AI_TRANSLATION_DEBUG=1`
  verbose tracing through every stage (closing the issue #218
  "Future work" item) and a `POLYSEMY_OVERRIDES` table that fixes
  noun↔verb homographs the Wikidata SPARQL lexeme join lands on the
  wrong side of (e.g. `milk → молоко` not `доить`, `water → вода` not
  `поливать`, `fish → рыба` not `рыбачить`).
- `tests/unit/specification/translation_via_links.rs` — three new
  regression tests covering quoted + unquoted common-noun translation
  in both directions.

### Offline cache
- `examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` — seed list expanded from
  one noun + greetings to **71 English nouns × 4 target languages + 71
  Russian nouns × 1 target**, built procedurally so future expansions
  stay readable.
- `data/translation-cache/` — refreshed snapshot (~3,200 new files)
  against the new seed list. Closes the
  `HttpError::Transport(... offline mode is active)` gap for every
  demo noun.

### Pre-compiled browser dictionary
- `examples/build_translation_dictionary.rs` (new) — replays the
  cached pipeline against the seed list and emits
  `src/web/translation-dictionary.json`. Includes a deterministic
  Russian declension table and English plural rules so inflected
  forms (`помидоры`, `tomatoes`) resolve without another lookup.
- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` — `loadTranslationDictionary()` fetches
  the JSON during `init()`; `translateSurface` consults
  `lookupDictionary(...)` before the hand-curated registry or the
  `[target] surface` placeholder.

### Tests & docs
- `tests/e2e/tests/issue-221.spec.js` (new) — Playwright coverage
  mirroring the Rust unit tests plus a `ru→en→ru` round-trip.
- `tests/unit/docs_requirements.rs` — skips `data/translation-cache/`
  so raw Wiktionary bodies (which contain ISO 639-3 language codes
  like `mvp` for Duri) don't trip the deferred-label scanner.
- `docs/case-studies/issue-221/{README.md,online-research.md,raw-data/*.txt}`
  — full case study with reproductions and provenance.

## Before / After

| Prompt | Before (v0.100.0) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Переведи "помидор" на английский.` | `"[en] помидор"` | `"tomato"` |
| `Переведи "огурец" на английский.` | `"[en] огурец"` | `"cucumber"` |
| `переведи "картофель" на английский` | `"[en] картофель"` | `"potato"` |
| `translate "tomato" to russian` | `"[ru] tomato"` | `"помидор"` |
| `translate "carrot" to russian` | `"[ru] carrot"` | `"морковь"` |
| `переведи помидор на английский` (unquoted) | `"[en] помидор"` | `"tomato"` |

[2026-05-22T01:05:25.275Z] [INFO]     "originalFile": "//! File-based cache for raw HTTP responses from Wikipedia / Wikidata /\n//! Wiktionary, keyed by the **semantic identity** of the resource.\n//!\n//! Earlier revisions of this module hashed the full URL and dumped 3 500+\n//! tiny `.body` / `.url` files into a single `data/translation-cache/`\n//! directory. That made the pull request unreviewable and locked the\n//! cache to one consumer (translation). Issue #221 reshaped the cache so\n//! that:\n//!\n//! - **Wikidata** responses land under `data/wikidata-cache/` keyed by\n//!   the Q-id or Lexeme-id mentioned in the URL.\n//! - **Wiktionary** wikitext lands under `data/wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`\n//!   keyed by the page title.\n//! - **SPARQL** queries land under `data/wikidata-cache/sparql/` keyed by\n//!   a short hash, because there is no natural semantic name for a SPARQL\n//!   string.\n//! - **Everything else** still uses a URL-hash filename, but in a\n//!   dedicated `data/http-cache/misc/` bucket. Unrecognised hosts should\n//!   be rare in practice — the cache is intentionally narrow.\n//!\n//! This layout lets other formalization paths reuse the same Wikidata or\n//! Wiktionary lookups without duplicating bytes. It also keeps each\n//! directory small and human-readable (`grep -R apple\n//! data/wiktionary-cache/` works).\n//!\n//! Cache contents are gitignored: they are populated lazily by integration\n//! runs (`FORMAL_AI_LIVE_API=1`) and serve only as a local accelerator.\n//! Unit tests rely on the offline dictionary at\n//! `data/seed/translations.lino`, not on cached HTTP responses, so the\n//! committed repository stays light.\n\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse super::http::{HttpClient, HttpError};\n\n/// Default cache root, relative to the crate root.\n///\n/// Per-source subfolders (`wikidata-cache/`, `wiktionary-cache/<lang>/`, …)\n/// live as siblings of this directory so callers from other formalization\n/// paths can share the same bytes.\npub const DEFAULT_CACHE_DIR: &str = \"data\";\n\n/// HTTP client that consults a file cache before delegating to a real\n/// transport. Cache hits always short-circuit the underlying transport;\n/// cache misses populate the cache after a successful fetch.\npub struct CachedHttpClient<T: HttpClient> {\n    cache_dir: PathBuf,\n    transport: T,\n    /// When `true`, cache misses fall through to the transport. When\n    /// `false`, cache misses return [`HttpError::Transport`] without any\n    /// network access.
